title: The car repair
prompt: Your car needs a $900 repair to remain reliable. You depend on it for work, but public transit is available with a longer commute.

choices.label: Pay for the repair
choices.text: Use $900 of cash to keep your usual commute.
choices.feedback: Your immediate cash fell. Reliable transport reduced uncertainty about getting to work.

choices.label: Use transit for now
choices.text: Spend $250 on short-term transit while you compare repair estimates.
choices.feedback: You kept more cash available but traded away commute time. The car still needs attention.

choices.label: Finance the repair
choices.text: Add $1,000 to debt, including the example financing cost.
choices.feedback: Your cash stayed available, but borrowing increased what you owe. In this model all debt uses the same simplified interest rule.

title: Your subscriptions add up
prompt: You discover $420 in annual subscriptions you barely use. One service is how you regularly connect with friends.

choices.label: Cancel the unused services
choices.text: Keep the social service and save $300 this year.
choices.feedback: You cut spending that mattered less while keeping a valued connection.

choices.label: Cancel all subscriptions
choices.feedback: You saved more money but lost a convenient way to connect with friends.

choices.label: Keep everything
choices.text: Choose convenience and revisit the list later.
choices.feedback: Nothing changed in your budget. Convenience used money you could have directed toward another goal.

title: Extra debt payment or cash buffer?
prompt: You have room to redirect $700. Your normal yearly debt payment will still be calculated at year-end.

choices.label: Pay extra toward debt
choices.text: Use up to $700 of available cash and your remaining debt balance.
choices.feedback: You traded some available cash for a lower debt balance. Only cash and debt actually available can be used.

choices.label: Keep an emergency buffer
choices.text: Leave the money in cash for unexpected expenses.
choices.feedback: Keeping cash available can prevent rushed borrowing. Your debt balance did not fall from this choice.

choices.label: Spend on a weekend away
choices.feedback: The break helped well-being, while reducing money available for future bills or debt.

title: The cheaper commute
prompt: A used bicycle and safety equipment cost $400. Cycling some days could save $650 in transport costs this year, but takes longer.

choices.label: Try the bicycle plan
choices.text: Pay $400 and make the trips that produce the $650 saving.
choices.feedback: The example net saving was $250 after equipment. The additional commute time was a separate cost.

choices.label: Share rides
choices.text: Coordinate rides and save $200 this year.
choices.feedback: Cooperation reduced costs, but you needed to coordinate schedules.

choices.label: Keep your current commute
choices.feedback: You kept a predictable routine and gave up the potential savings.

title: A tempting purchase
prompt: A new device costs $1,200. Your current device still works, but the upgrade would be enjoyable.

choices.label: Buy it now
choices.feedback: You enjoyed the upgrade and had less cash for other priorities.

choices.label: Choose a refurbished model
choices.feedback: You met part of the want at a lower cost. The $450 still had an opportunity cost.

choices.label: Keep what works
choices.text: Delay the purchase and keep your cash.
choices.feedback: You preserved financial flexibility but postponed something you wanted.

title: Share a professional membership?
prompt: An optional professional association offers workshops and networking for $350 a year. Your employer will reimburse $200 if you document what you learn.

choices.label: Join and document the learning
choices.text: Pay the $150 net cost and attend workshops.
choices.feedback: Employer support reduced the cash cost. Participation still required your time.

choices.label: Use free local events
choices.text: Attend a few free events instead.
choices.feedback: You made connections without a membership fee, with fewer structured resources.

choices.label: Skip networking this year
choices.feedback: You protected time and cash while passing up these particular learning opportunities.
